learningObjective: Understand CUDA Graph lifecycle: capture → instantiate → repeated launch; benefit is CPU-side overhead reduction.

canonicalClaims.claim: A CUDA Graph captures a DAG of GPU ops that is instantiated to an executable graph launchable many times, drastically reducing per-launch CPU overhead. It does not modify individual kernel bodies or change per-kernel GPU cost.
conditions: Standard CUDA Graph API; benefit visible when many short kernels dominate.
nonImplications: Does not imply gains for long-running kernels.
Does not imply zero per-launch cost.

misconceptions.claim: CUDA Graphs speed up individual kernels' GPU execution.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The savings are CPU-side (launch overhead); kernel body is unchanged.

misconceptions.claim: An instantiated graph can only be launched once.
misconceptions.whyWrong: It can be launched arbitrarily many times.

misconceptions.claim: Graphs and Streams are the same mechanism.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Streams sequence ops; graphs capture and re-launch DAGs.

misconceptions.claim: Any workload benefits from CUDA Graphs.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Long, launch-overhead-insignificant kernels see little benefit.

performanceScenarios: LLM decoding, RNN inference, and any per-step short-kernel loops are canonical wins for CUDA Graph.
